title: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5.5
gist: Anthropic launches Claude Sonnet 5.5, a mid-tier model that is 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper per task than Sonnet 5 at unchanged list prices, scoring 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 and near Opus 5.5 on knowledge work. It ships with new cyber and anti-distillation safeguards, while Opus 5.5 stays ahead on open-ended judgment.

insights.claim: Claude Sonnet 5.5 is positioned as a faster, lower-cost complement to Claude Opus 5.5: Opus for complex work needing careful judgment, Sonnet for well-scoped everyday tasks, bug fixing and polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, with Haiku 5.5 due within weeks.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Tiered model lineup lets buyers route work by difficulty; a Haiku 5.5 launch is the next catalyst for high-volume, cost-sensitive workloads.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 keeps Sonnet 5 list pricing ($2 per million input, $10 output, $0.20 cache reads) but needs far fewer tokens per task, cutting cost per task by up to 30%, so the price cut is delivered through token efficiency rather than list price.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Effective unit economics fall without list-price changes; watch cost-per-task rather than per-token price when comparing vendors.

insights.claim: Opus 5.5 is priced at exactly twice Sonnet 5.5 on input ($4 vs $2), output ($20 vs $10) and cache writes ($5 vs $2.50), while cache reads are equal at $0.20 per million tokens.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Sets a clear 2x premium for the top tier; cache-read parity favors long-context agent workloads on either model.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 generates output 30%+ faster than Sonnet 5, making it the fastest Sonnet model to date.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Latency gains matter for interactive products and agent loops where speed drives adoption.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 scores 70.6% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 10.3% for Sonnet 5 and 66.4% for Opus 5.5 (at Xhigh), an agentic coding jump large enough that the mid-tier model beats the flagship on this test.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Suggests the mid-tier now covers most agentic terminal work, pressuring premium-tier pricing power and rival coding agents.

insights.claim: At lower effort settings Sonnet 5.5 beats Sonnet 5's best score on several benchmarks for about a tenth of the cost per task, and at High effort on FrontierCode it matches GPT-6 Sol's best score for about a fifth of the cost.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Capability per dollar is the competitive axis; Anthropic claims a large cost advantage over OpenAI at equal coding scores.

insights.claim: On GDPval-AA, a test of real-world tasks across 44 occupations, Sonnet 5.5 is nearly level with Opus 5.5 (1844 vs 1846) and about 400 points above Sonnet 5 (1449), and it clearly outperforms Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Sol on long-horizon knowledge work (AA-Briefcase).
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Knowledge-work automation (analysts, office tasks) is reaching near-flagship quality at mid-tier cost, widening the addressable enterprise use cases.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 scores 61.6% on the Chartography chart-recognition benchmark versus 15.6% for Sonnet 5 and 53.6% for GPT-6 Sol, and 80.1% on OSWorld 2.1 computer use versus 57.0% for Sonnet 5.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Vision and computer-use gains open finance and back-office automation where reading charts and driving GUIs is the bottleneck.

insights.claim: Anthropic concedes benchmarks capture only one facet: Opus 5.5 remains clearly stronger at complex, open-ended work requiring sustained judgment, even though Sonnet 5.5 at Max effort matches it on several evaluations.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The premium tier keeps a defensible niche in judgment-heavy work; do not extrapolate benchmark parity to all workloads.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 scores lower at Max effort than at Xhigh on FrontierCode because it more often invoked Claude Code's code-review skill, which spawns many subagents and led to timeouts or out-of-scope edits that the benchmark penalizes.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: More effort and more subagents can reduce score on scope-sensitive tasks; agent orchestration has failure modes that hurt reliability.

insights.claim: Base44 reports that across 118 real app builds Sonnet 5.5 matched Opus 5 quality in 3.6 iterations per build versus 7.7 for Opus 5, with the fewest failed tool calls of any model compared and rare mid-build stalls to ask questions.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Iteration count is a direct cost and latency driver for app-builder products; fewer loops improve margins for vibe-coding platforms.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 batches tool calls more than Sonnet 5, and Lovable measured a third fewer tool calls and about half the shell runs to finish a task, while CodeRabbit says the old habit of over-using web search and high token use are gone.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Efficiency gains at the agent-loop level compound into lower inference cost for customers building on the API.

insights.claim: SpaceXAI says Sonnet 5.5 hits 55.5% on CursorBench 4.0, second only to Opus 5.5, and Epic Games reports it handled tens of thousands of lines of gameplay architecture code and multi-hour tasks with less prescriptive prompting.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Game and dev-tool companies are validating mid-tier models for long-horizon work, an adoption signal for AI coding spend.

insights.claim: A workable division of labor is emerging in which Opus 5.5 sets architecture and Sonnet 5.5 implements it, per an early tester's remark that he would feel confident letting Sonnet 5.5 implement what Opus 5.5 designs.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Multi-model routing (expensive planner, cheap executor) shifts token demand toward the lower-priced tier.

insights.claim: Balyasny Asset Management ran 2,441 finance tasks and found Sonnet 5.5 beat Sonnet 5 while using about 121k tokens per answer versus 497k, with the best quality-to-cost tradeoff of seven models tested for high-volume workflows.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A large multi-strategy fund is quantifying roughly 4x token savings; buy-side adoption of LLM research workflows is cost-driven and accelerating.

insights.claim: Box says Sonnet 5.5 was more accurate, 2.4x faster and used 12% fewer tokens than the prior model, and re-checks data in source documents to catch errors Sonnet 5 missed, supporting use in financial services and healthcare.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Verification behavior is what regulated industries need before deploying; it supports enterprise content-management AI attach rates.

insights.claim: Enterprise software vendors report concrete speedups: Zendesk saw tickets processed 20% faster with fewer wrong decisions, Slack saw about 14% fewer output tokens, and Atlassian expects Rovo agents to run up to 30% faster.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: SaaS incumbents are embedding the model into agents at scale, tying their unit economics to Anthropic model efficiency.

insights.claim: In an internal test, Sonnet 5.5 was given a public company's quarterly earnings materials, call transcripts and a slide template to produce a 10-slide operating review, and two experts judged the first draft ready to send as is.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Routine analyst deliverables such as earnings decks are becoming automatable, a pressure point for junior finance workloads.

insights.claim: Because Sonnet 5.5's cyber capabilities are comparable to Opus 5's, it is the first Sonnet model to ship with cyber safeguards and fallbacks; higher-risk cybersecurity tasks visibly fall back to Sonnet 5, and defenders can apply to a Cyber Verification Program for tiered access.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Capability growth in a cheaper model now triggers gated access; cyber-defense vendors may gain tiered access while offensive use is restricted.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 is the first Sonnet model to launch with classifiers that prevent reasoning extraction and expands preserved thinking so thinking cannot be decoupled from the originating account, a defense against distillation attacks using thousands of fake accounts.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Model-capability theft via distillation is treated as a core moat risk; watch for account-portability friction and effects on competitors building on extracted outputs.
insights.quote: Distillation attacks, in which attackers use thousands of fake accounts to extract a model’s capabilities at industrial scale

insights.claim: On an automated audit of roughly 1,850 scenarios Sonnet 5.5 improves on or matches Sonnet 5 on most alignment measures and is the least likely of any Anthropic model to probe container limits, though Anthropic warns no evaluation reliably catches every failure.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Alignment evidence is a procurement input for enterprises; the admitted evaluation gaps keep tail-risk in view.

insights.claim: Sonnet 5.5 is available on all major clouds (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure) and the Claude Platform as claude-sonnet-5-5 with zero data retention; developers running with thinking off must move to a new between_tools setting before migrating.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Multi-cloud day-one distribution supports hyperscaler AI revenue; the breaking thinking-setting change creates migration work for API users.

insights.claim: Default effort is Medium in Claude Code and the Claude apps but High on the Claude Platform, and Anthropic frames effort level as the main dial trading cost and speed against quality.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Effort tiers make per-task cost variable; usage-based revenue depends on which default customers accept.
